name: NRF homepage: the National Retail Federation's retail industry landing page
title: NRF homepage: the National Retail Federation's retail industry landing page
answer: This is the homepage of the National Retail Federation, a retail trade body that describes itself as standing up for the people, policies and ideas that help retail thrive, and offering retail news, insights and industry events. Its most useful line for AI readers is a short note that conversations in Paris moved from practical AI to connected stores and relationship-driven loyalty, framed as retailers turning The Next Now into action. Beyond that the page is a signpost, not a study, and carries no data.

sections.body: This is the homepage of the National Retail Federation, published by the National Retail Federation itself. It is not a report, an article or a research paper, it is the organisation's own front page, and its stated scope is retail news, insights and industry events. No publication date, author or report title is given in the harvested text. The only date attached to it is the harvest date of 27 September 2026, which is when the page was captured rather than when it was written or updated.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page carries two short blocks of text. The first is a description of the organisation, stating that the National Retail Federation stands up for the people, policies and ideas that help retail thrive, and that it offers retail news, insights and industry events. That description is repeated, so the page effectively says the same thing twice. The second block is a single line about an event in Paris, which states that conversations there moved from practical AI to connected stores and relationship-driven loyalty, and that these conversations showed how retailers are turning The Next Now into action. No further detail is given about who spoke, which retailers took part, what was demonstrated, or what The Next Now refers to. There is no article, report, survey or dataset on the page as harvested. Nothing here defines store automation, inventory computer vision or customer-experience software, and no adoption figures appear. A reader looking for the trade body's research output would have to go further into the site, because the homepage itself only names the topics and points to news, insights and events.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, no dates and no definitions. Its only substantive claims are that the National Retail Federation stands up for the people, policies and ideas that help retail thrive, that it offers retail news, insights and industry events, and that conversations in Paris moved from practical AI to connected stores and relationship-driven loyalty, described as retailers turning The Next Now into action.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in retail would use this page only as a pointer. It confirms that the National Retail Federation presents itself as a retail trade body whose output covers news, insights and events, and it names practical AI, connected stores and relationship-driven loyalty as themes retailers are acting on. That is useful for knowing where retail AI coverage is likely to sit and which organisation produces it. It is not useful as evidence of adoption, because the page offers no counts, no survey results and no case detail. Anyone citing it for adoption numbers would be citing a homepage that does not contain them.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Retail

sections.body: This is a landing page with very little substance. It has no date, no author, no methodology and no data. It is the trade body's own promotional front page, so it presents the organisation in its own terms rather than offering independent assessment. It does not cover store automation, inventory computer vision or customer-experience software in any detail, and it does not report adoption rates. The Paris reference is a single sentence with no supporting article attached in the harvested text. The page is current only as of the harvest date, and its content may change without notice.
